strengths: Idempotent unique lookup via order_id with lockForUpdate and unique DB constraint; reuse path correctly reuses existing invoice without duplicate creation (InvoiceBackfillService.php:56-59,68)
Chunked bounded processing via Order::chunkById with configurable --chunk option and explicit validation (InvoiceBackfillService.php:42-44, BackfillInvoices.php:19-26)

Per-row failure visibility with try/catch per order, onRow callback reporting created/reused/skipped/failed events and explicit command counters with FAILURE exit when failed>0 (InvoiceBackfillService.php:52-79, BackfillInvoices.php:28-42)

No synthetic payment mutation: payments only read via sum where status=completed and amount>0; never creates or modifies Payment rows (InvoiceBackfillService.php:101-107); verified zero Payment::create/update in scope

Deterministic dates delegated to InvoiceService::createForApprovedOrder using Carbon::today() and outlet effectivePaymentTermDays with 7-day fallback; due-date logic verified in test via 14-day diff assertion

Transaction boundary correctness: per-row DB::transaction enclosing order lock, invoice lookup/creation, and synchronizeAmounts update atomically; failure rolls back single row without aborting remaining chunk
Additive-only behavior confirmed: no DELETE/TRUNCATE/destroy, no destructive cleanup, no automatic web-request invocation; command is admin-controlled Artisan only
All three RED/GREEN scenarios exercised through real Artisan and database with no application mocks; 3 passed, 31 assertions green

issues.description: backfill() is 56 lines (29-84) marginally over the ~50-line heuristic; method remains cohesive as a chunk-orchestrator with predicates and counters co-located per quality bar, so no split is mandated — consider extracting per-order processing to a private method if the method grows further

hasInvoiceNumberConflict() queries without row lock inside the per-row transaction; race is ultimately guarded by the invoices.invoice_number unique constraint and outer Throwable catch (counted as failed), but an explicit lock or relying solely on constraint exception handling would make the intent clearer

Deterministic issue/due dates use Carbon::today() directly; tests pin to today consistently and are green, but injecting a clock or Carbon::setTestNow would make date-dependent behavior more explicit for future time-sensitive tests
